hook
Every time you pump RON ninety-five at one ringgit ninety-nine, the government quietly pays the rest.
real
This week, the real, unsubsidised price is about four ringgit sixty.
gap
That means roughly two ringgit sixty of every litre is paid with public money.
cost
This year, fuel subsidies could cost forty billion ringgit. That's over a thousand ringgit for every Malaysian.
why
Why so much? Conflict in West Asia pushed oil above a hundred and twenty US dollars a barrel.
twist
But here's the controversial part. The more petrol you burn, the more subsidy you get.
Back in 2022, the government said that for every ringgit of fuel subsidy, fifty-three sen went to the richest twenty percent. Only fifteen sen reached the poorest forty.
budi
That's why BUDI ninety-five exists. Only Malaysians with a driving licence get the cheap price, up to three hundred litres a month.
flip
But cut subsidies too hard, and transport, food, and almost everything else gets more expensive, hitting the poorest families first.
outro
So, should petrol subsidies be cut further? Tell me in the comments, and follow The Common Cents for more money, explained.
